alignments.note: Waw rendered *Thus* (rule 14's open list).
Passive recasting; the auxiliary joins the verb's unit (rule 17), discontinuous around the subject pronoun under rule 25.
The object suffix is promoted to the English subject pronoun of the passive (rule 18).
Instrumental בְּ → *by*.
The ASV writes the singular *lot* for the plural גּוֹרָלוֹת; it is the noun's own word either way.

The demonstrative is rendered by the contrastive *one*, with *sort* supplied to complete the English phrase; the head stays on the word carrying the contrastive force and not on the supplied generic (rule 31).
עִם → *with*.
The second demonstrative takes the answering *another*.
כִּי → *for*.
Existential הָיָה takes *there were*, the dummy subject belonging to the verb (rule 21).
Construct noun keeps only its own word (rule 19).

Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19); no article morpheme stands in the phrase, and the single written *the* stands before this word, so it is the supplied determiner of this nominal expression (rules 15, 29).
Waw takes the *and* written for it.
Second construct noun keeps only its own word.
The ASV writes *of God* with no article (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).

Partitive מִן → *of*. The opening *both* is not this morpheme's: rule 14 gives another morpheme the opening correlative only where that morpheme is itself what the correlative says — a present negative for *neither*, or the מִן of a מִן…עַד range for *both* — and this is a partitive preposition standing before one of two coordinated phrases, not a range. A morpheme that merely stands where the opener stands has no claim on it, and this one already holds the *of* the ASV wrote for it.
Construct noun with supplied *the* (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).

One connective morpheme rendered by the correlative pair *both … and*: both English words belong to this waw's one discontinuous unit, headed on the closing connective (rules 14, 25). The competing reading gives *both* to the מִן as the phrase's opener, but position is not what allocates the word, and rule 51's limit expressly excepts a correlative pair from the count that would otherwise bar a morpheme from holding two words.
בְּ rendered *of* in the second member (rule 11).
Construct noun with supplied *the* (rule 29).
Rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19).

review_notes: Corrected: the correlative *both … and* is the waw's one discontinuous unit (rule 14), headed on *and*. The accepted alignment gave *both* to the partitive מִן, but rule 14's carve-out reaches only a morpheme that is itself what the opening correlative says — its named instance is the מִן of a מִן…עַד range — and this clause coordinates two partitive phrases with no range in it.
The מִן keeps the *of* written for it; only *both* moves, so the phrase's two connectives are counted against the two morphemes that could carry them (rule 42's method).
